points.description: Core fact: selection sort repeatedly finds the minimum (smallest) element of the remaining unsorted elements.
The minimum is swapped with the current element at the left/front of the unsorted portion, i.e. the element being processed (position being filled), so the sorted part grows from left to right.
points.partial_credit: Half a mark for mentioning a swap or exchange of the minimum with the current position without saying which position it goes to.

points.description: Distinction from the related idea: the process takes elements one at a time from left to right (current position moves through the array), rather than sorting by repeated comparison of adjacent pairs or by inserting into a sorted part.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the minimum of the remaining (unsorted) elements, swapped with the current element, and the left-to-right processing order, all stated precisely with the terms "minimum" and "swap". Part marks (P2 only) are for naming the swap without saying which position the minimum goes to. Vague wording such as "sorts the array" or "puts elements in order" earns nothing for the core point, and a statement that the minimum is found but no swap is described earns no marks for P2.
